messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: 
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Surge Protection + Price Anchoring for Renewal

Hi Sasha —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. As NebulaHealth approaches the end of the current term, I put together a short proposal intended to balance your need for predictable unit economics while giving you runway to scale without surprise overruns. Key idea: combine a price-anchoring commitment with a small surge-protection buffer (credits) and a two-quarter true-up cadence.

Attachment: 20270620-draft-pricing-matrix.xlsx (pricing bands, commit levels, and sample invoices)

High level options (short):
- Option A (Conservative): 12-month renewal, 10% commit uplift, 6-month price hold on base rate, 5% surge credit pool (apply to overage within quarter)
- Option B (Aggressive scaling): 18-month renewal, 25% commit uplift, 9-month price hold, 3% surge credit + discounted onboarding credits for the first 90 days
- Technical add-on: Dedicated onboarding credits (2 FTE-weeks of SRE support, applied as credit)

Please review and tell me which direction you prefer — I can formalize the term sheet and loop in procurement for counters. If you prefer, we can do a short call this week (30 minutes) to walk through numbers.

Best,
David
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nebulahealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Surge Protection + Price Anchoring for Renewal

Thanks, David.

Appreciate the clear options — procurement and I ran some numbers. A couple of constraints from our end:
- We cannot commit to a 25% uplift up front (Option B) without a usage forecast tied to a milestone.
- Procurement prefers semi-annual true-ups instead of quarterly, to simplify billing cycles.
- We like the idea of a price hold but need an explicit cap on the maximum discount across the full term (so we can model long-term TCO).

A few asks: 
1) Can you provide a middle-ground Option C that has a staged uplift (10% first 6 months, additional 10% after hitting agreed usage milestone at month 9)?
2) Can the surge credit be used across two consecutive quarters if we underspend in the first one?
3) Please send any legal/term language about price anchoring and the triggers for the true-up. Procurement would like to see explicit billing examples.

If helpful, our procurement rep (cc'd) can share the standard PO terms we need on file. We can block a 30-minute slot tomorrow afternoon for a walkthrough.

Best,
Sasha
VP Product Operations, NebulaHealth
---

Sasha —

Thanks for the quick read and helpful constraints. I put together Option C inline and attached a short term-sheet that maps triggers to concrete invoice examples.

Attachment: 20270621-surge-protection-term-sheet.pdf (Option definitions + sample invoice flows)

Option C (Staged uplift + milestone):
- Term: 15 months
- Commit: +10% baseline for months 1–6, additional +10% from month 10 onward if Usage Milestone = 60% of projected monthly tokens for two consecutive months (months 8–9 review window)
- Price hold: 6 months guaranteed base rate; after month 6, July 1 pricing applies to new baseline only
- Surge protection: 5% credit pool (rolls forward one quarter only; exception: if underspend >= 80% of pool, remaining credit can be applied to following quarter once per 12-month term)
- True-up cadence: semi-annual (aligned with Sasha's ask)
- Onboarding credit: 2-week SRE support (applied as a $15k credit against first invoice)
- Discount guardrails: max effective discount across term capped at 12% (we need approval for anything beyond this)

Next steps: 
- If this looks directionally correct, I can produce a redline-friendly PDF and loop in legal for a narrow amendment.
- Also cc'ing Marissa for quick alignment on discount guardrail — Marissa, can we approve up to 12% for DEAL-3869 or do we need an uplift approval path?

Happy to hop on a 30-min tomorrow at 3pm PT to walk procurement through the invoice samples.

Best,
David
